Title: June 18, 2026 - Regular Meeting of the Boulder City Council

Topic1.Title: Call to Order and Agenda Amendment
Topic1.Summary: Mayor Brockett called the regular meeting to order and conducted roll call, with all members present. Council voted 8-0 to add item 3B, the Colorado Music Festival's 50th anniversary declaration, to the agenda. The meeting then moved to open comment.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment Public Testimony
Topic2.Summary: Roughly twenty speakers addressed Council in two-minute slots on topics including Ponderosa Mobile Home Park redevelopment, proposed changes to the tip credit and minimum wage, the Fort Chambers interpretive design, Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan notification, the Downtown DDA's revenue impacts, and Israel and Gaza. Speakers also raised concerns about racism and antisemitism in the community, along with a dispute involving a former resident. The Mayor cut off speakers who exceeded their time or made personal attacks.

Topic3.Title: Staff Responses and Council Questions on Public Comment
Topic3.Summary: Staff committed to follow up on Fort Chambers concerns, Ponderosa resident issues, and the DDA, which returns to Council on August 6. Assistant City Manager Mark Wolf described outreach for the tip credit proposal, which returns July 30. Council Member Adams asked about the racial equity tool and investment portfolio complaints, and staff said the investment concerns are under internal review. Council Member Adams shared a personal account of a racial slur and urged more action on public safety, and Council members condemned the harassment of Jewish students and residents.

Topic4.Title: Juneteenth Declaration
Topic4.Summary: Council Member Kaplan presented a declaration recognizing Juneteenth 2026 and its historical significance as the commemoration of the end of chattel slavery in the United States. The declaration encourages community members to attend local Juneteenth events and affirms the City's opposition to oppression. Dr. David Lewis Humphrey, who spoke at a Juneteenth event, received the declaration.

Topic5.Title: Colorado Music Festival 50th Anniversary Declaration
Topic5.Summary: Council Member Marquis presented a declaration celebrating the Colorado Music Festival's 50th season, which runs July 9 through August 9 at Chautauqua Auditorium. The declaration designates July 9, 2026 as Colorado Music Festival Day in Boulder. Festival representative Elizabeth accepted the declaration and thanked Council for its support of the arts.

Topic6.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic6.Summary: Council considered consent agenda items 4A through 4D together. A motion and second were made to approve the consent agenda. The items were approved unanimously on roll call vote.

Topic7.Title: Call-Up Check-Ins
Topic7.Summary: Council reviewed call-up items 5A and 5B. Item 5A is a concept plan to redevelop the Unity Church property at 2855 Folsom with 21 detached dwelling units. Item 5B is a landmark alteration certificate to demolish an accessory building at 1039 Mapleton Avenue in the Mapleton Hill Historic District. No Council member called either item up for further discussion.

Topic8.Title: Spring Valley Estates Annexation and Water Agreement
Topic8.Summary: Council adopted Resolution 1381, which finds that the proposed annexation of about 43 acres and 36 lots in Spring Valley Estates meets state law, sets additional terms and conditions, and directs an election. Council also unanimously authorized the City Manager to execute an agreement with Spring Valley Mutual Water Association for the transition of water services. The terms require a city water system, funded through a local improvement district, and no additional dwelling units may be added. Staff noted that a DOLA grant requires annexation by November 14, 2026, and that the 90-day election blackout may require waiver or an extension. Residents raised concerns about cost allocation fairness and a potential conflict of interest involving a parcel of land.

Topic9.Title: Ordinance 8751: Special Festival Event Regulations
Topic9.Summary: Planning staff presented Ordinance 8751, which creates a permit process and standards for large special festival events such as the 2027 Sundance Film Festival. The ordinance also amends mobile food vehicle rules and sign regulations for temporary festival signage. The Planning Board unanimously recommended approval, and staff will monitor the ordinance's effectiveness after the first festival. One speaker opposed the festival, and Council adopted the ordinance unanimously, effective in 30 days.

Topic10.Title: Ordinance 8752: Festival Liquor Licenses and Permits
Topic10.Summary: Regulatory Licensing Manager Alisa Darrow presented Ordinance 8752, which allows festival liquor licenses and permits authorized by state law since 2018. The ordinance establishes a $150 local application fee to recover administrative review costs and makes code cleanup changes to align with state statutes. Council discussed whether fees should be tied to cost recovery or revenue, and staff explained that the fee is based on processing time. Council adopted the ordinance unanimously.

Topic11.Title: Council Employee Evaluation Timeline and Adjournment
Topic11.Summary: Council Member Spear outlined the timeline for the 2026 council employee evaluation process. The survey opens July 7 and closes July 28, with results due August 10 and summaries completed by August 17 and shared by August 21. Any merit increases will be retroactive to July 1 and are expected to appear on the September 3 consent agenda. The Mayor then adjourned the meeting at 8:27 p.m.
